steps.title: Prepare the fractions
steps.note: Both values use the same-sized whole.

steps.title: Use a common denominator
steps.note: Both denominators are 7, so the parts already have equal size. Keep this denominator.

steps.title: Simplify
steps.note: Divide top and bottom by a common factor until none remains. An equivalent mixed number is also valid.

hint: The parts are already the same size: 7 per whole. Which numbers count how many parts you have?
method_note: Use denominator 7: 1/7 + 2/7. Combine the numerators, then simplify.
error_note: The denominator counts equal-sized parts. Do not add denominators or change a denominator without changing its numerator.

steps.title: Prepare the fractions
steps.note: Both values use the same-sized whole.

steps.title: Use a common denominator
steps.note: Use 6 equal parts per whole. Multiply each numerator and denominator by the same factor.

steps.title: Simplify
steps.note: Divide top and bottom by a common factor until none remains. An equivalent mixed number is also valid.

hint: What common multiple of 3 and 6 can be the denominator for both fractions?
method_note: Use denominator 6: 2/6 + 1/6. Combine the numerators, then simplify.
error_note: The denominator counts equal-sized parts. Do not add denominators or change a denominator without changing its numerator.
